title: Why 4 Small Payments Can Eat Half Your Paycheck
summary: Zoe, 19, splits five holiday purchases into "pay in 4" plans and never pays a cent of interest, yet by January $300 is due every two weeks, half her paycheck. This video covers seven things to understand before you tap buy now, pay later: the two kinds of plans, counting the whole stack, autopay dates and overdraft and late fees, why stores offer it, returns, credit reporting, and saving first, plus an honest comparison with a credit card balance. Examples assume $600 take-home pay every two weeks, $380 of regular costs, a $27 overdraft fee, an $8 late fee, a 30% APR monthly plan and a 22.36% card rate; they are illustrations, not predictions. Zoe and Sam are fictional composites.
